fieldDescription: This adds an Optimal entry to the autofit goals for every ship on the refit screen. The other goals still use the game's own autofit, so nothing changes there.

fieldName: Fit for each ship's fleet role
fieldDescription: Each ship gets fitted for the job it's actually good at in a fleet, going off its designation and its numbers (skirmisher frigates, flankers, brawlers, line cruisers, capital anchors, carriers, battle carriers, support, phase and missile boats). Speed compared to other ships its size counts too, so slow frigates and destroyers end up brawling and really fast cruisers flank. The role decides who it mostly fights, how much firepower it trades for staying alive, speed, how much outrunning its targets keeps it alive, range, point defense and fighters. If you turn it off, every ship just gets built as a generic duelist.

fieldName: Civilian ships: fit for the campaign
fieldDescription: Freighters, tankers, liners, salvage and survey ships never really fight, so they don't get weapons and they get campaign hullmods instead (cargo, fuel or berths depending on the ship, then burn speed, sensor profile, sensors, survey and salvage gear, treasure hunting and supply use). Any OP that's left over goes into vents and capacitors. You'll need a spaceport to add the hullmods.

fieldName: Civilian ships: build in fleet-wide hullmods
fieldDescription: With Build in s-mods ticked, the civilian ships you're keeping for good (cruisers and capitals like the Atlas and Prometheus, plus salvage rigs) build in the hullmods that help the whole fleet: Treasure Hunt Package, Surveying Equipment, High Resolution Sensors, then burn speed. It works in a single refit and in Optimize fleet, and it only spends story points when you hit Confirm. Built-in ones don't count against the logistics limit, so cargo, fuel or berths still fit. This is the starting value for a save; Optimize fleet has its own Civilian box under S-mods for each save.

Optimal looks at the rest of your fleet when it fits a ship. Fighter roles you've already got covered (fighters, bombers, interceptors, support) and duplicate wings count for less, and with the Auto or Balanced style each ship leans toward whatever damage the fleet is short on (anti-shield or anti-armor). Basically the fleet as a whole ends up being the all-rounder. Optimize fleet balances each ship against the plan for the others, and a single Optimal fit balances against your fleet as it is right now.

The ship you're flying gets fitted so it can do everything on its own. Its role's damage focus goes halfway to even, it fights every ship size, it carries its own point defense (at least 1.2x what it needs), it has kinetic and armor-cracking damage, and capitals get a little more survival. It still keeps its role though (a carrier is still a carrier). Optimize fleet plans it first so it gets first pick of the weapons.

secondaryValue: Auto, Balanced, Anti-shield, Anti-armor, Hull killer
fieldDescription: Auto picks a style for each ship based on its slots and role. Balanced covers all three layers, so it breaks shields, strips armor and kills hull. The other styles put most of the firepower into one layer and keep enough of the rest to finish the job.
This also adds Optimal (Balanced), (Anti-shield), (Anti-armor) and (Hull killer) goals, so you can give each ship its own style.
Auto goes off the ship itself (speed, armor, slot arcs). Long keeps every gun close to the longest range, and Close cares more about damage than range.
How long a typical fight lasts, in seconds. Short fights favor burst damage and missiles, and longer ones favor flux-efficient sustained fire.
This counts scripted effects (EMP arcs, shield piercing, damage over time, chain hits) on top of the plain numbers, so rare weapons win when they're actually stronger.
Gives rarer weapons (lower drop rate, higher tier, rare blueprints) a bonus on top of how strong they measure. If it's off, weapons only win on measured strength (special effects included).

fieldName: Use items you can only get with cheats
fieldDescription: If it's off, weapons and LPCs that have no blueprint, that no NPC faction knows and that no ship in any mod carries (console allweapons stuff like Yunru's gyrojets) get left out of fits, Optimize fleet and fleet orders. Omega, Threat and Dweller gear always counts, since you can actually get those in a game.

When two weapons score about the same, the one the community rates higher for AI ships wins (Grievous69's 0.98a tier lists, so Burst PD beats LR PD and HVD beats Gauss). It only moves a weapon's value by about 5%% at most. It's vanilla weapons only, but other mods can add rows to data/config/jao_weapon_tiers.csv.
How much of a bonus the rarest weapon gets when Prefer rare weapons is on (0.15 = +15%%). Less rare ones get a smaller one.
Weapons and fighters you've marked as priority in your faction doctrine win if they score within 1%% of the best other pick for a mount. The game's own refit autofit just ignores those marks.

A weapon or LPC from a market has to make the ship this much stronger for every 10,000 credits it costs, compared to what you already own (0.01 = 1%% per 10,000 credits). Survival mode prices weapons x10 and LPCs x5. At 0 it ignores prices. Order fleet weapons never buys from markets, and Optimize fleet only buys when its shop ticks are on.
How much point defense a ship needs for its size. At 1 it's enough to stop a typical missile volley, and at 0 it doesn't need any.
Weapon ids or patterns, separated by commas (stardust_* skips every Stardust Ventures weapon). The Optimal fit will never pick these.

If it's off, it only uses hullmods that don't make anything about the ship worse (no lost range, speed, handling, shield or flux, no higher supply, recovery, deployment, crew or crew salary cost, and no s-mod penalty). If it's on, drawbacks get weighed against what they gain in battle (supply, deployment and salary costs aren't scored). Safety Overrides needs this on.

If it's off, Shrouded Mantle, Lens and Thunderhead never get added (any already on a ship stay). If it's on, they're scored by the damage they deal and used where they add the most, crew casualties +50%% included. Keep in mind a fleet with a Shrouded hullmod makes the Luddic Path, the Luddic Church and the Knights of Ludd hostile when they see it.

secondaryValue: Never, Frigates and destroyers, When it scores best
fieldDescription: Safety Overrides doubles dissipation, but it cuts range past 450, cuts peak time by two thirds and stops venting. On 0.98.5a it also adds crew losses by peak time used and doubles the ship's crew salary. Frigates and destroyers means only on those, and only when it really scores best (short-range guns). When it scores best means any hull the game allows.
If it's off, it never adds hullmods that only help in the campaign (cargo, fuel, sensors, burn).

If you've got AI Tweaks, this puts its Custom AI hullmod on every capital. It costs no OP, so it never pushes anything else off. Custom AI puts a ship on Search and Destroy, and cruisers with it kept diving into the enemy line, so cruisers get it taken off when they're refitted. Frigates and destroyers stay the way they are.

The most new s-mods it'll build into a ship in one Optimal fit or one Optimize fleet, within the ship's own s-mod limit. Optimal only builds s-mods when the Autofit box "Build in s-mods" is ticked, and Optimize fleet has its own "Build in s-mods" tick.
The most story points one Optimize fleet will spend in total, warships first. At 0 there's no limit, so it spends down to Story points to keep.
How much stronger an s-mod has to make the ship before it's worth a story point (0.02 = 2%%).

If a clearly better set of s-mods needs hullmods you don't know yet, or ones you can only fit at a spaceport, it holds those slots open for them. The other slots still get the best you have, and the log says what's being held.

fieldName: How much better to wait for
fieldDescription: It only waits when the best possible s-mods are at least this much better than the best you've got now (0.1 = 10%%).

fieldName: Most days to hold a slot
fieldDescription: Once a ship has held s-mod slots this many days waiting on a missing hullmod, it just builds the best you have into them.
It never spends your story points below this number, so you always have some left for yourself.

The minimum gain per s-mod gets multiplied by 20 / the ship's deployment points, from 0.5x to 4x, so a 5 DP frigate needs 4x the gain and a 40 DP capital only 0.5x. This is so your story points mostly go to the bigger ships.
The most s-mods it'll build into a frigate (any s-mods already on the ship count toward that).
The most s-mods it'll build into a destroyer (any s-mods already on the ship count toward that).

This is for Optimize fleet with "Change s-mods with credits" ticked. Swapping out or removing an s-mod has to make the ship at least this much stronger (0.1 = 10%%), and it scales by ship size the same way the minimum gain per s-mod does.

Puts a button on the refit screen (and in LunaLib's refit menu) that plans every ship's Optimal fit with all the weapon and fighter blueprints you know, lists what custom production would have to build, and queues it up when you hit Queue all. Turning it off only hides this button.

How much of your credits one fleet order is allowed to cost (0.5 = half). The order is always the whole fleet's plan, and whatever doesn't fit the budget (smaller ships go last) gets ordered the next time you hit the button.

For Random Assortment of Things. A Frontiers settlement with Ordnance Manufacturing takes the biggest ships' items up to its budget, at its own prices, and you pay when you order. The rest goes to custom production.
Writes each Optimal fit's scores and reasons to starsector.log, which is mainly useful if you're reporting a bug.

fieldName: Debug: remove all s-mods and refund story points
fieldDescription: Turn it on in a game and save the settings. Every ship in your fleet loses its s-mods, built-in hullmods lose their s-mod bonus, and you get one story point back for each s-mod (you keep the bonus XP from building them). It runs once each time you turn it on, so turn it back off afterwards.
